questions.question: Why is lattice energy not measured directly, and how does the Born- Haber cycle help determine it? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Why is lattice energy not measured directly and how does the Born Haber cycle help to determine it?
  • Ans: Lattice energy is the energy released when one mole of an ionic compound in crystalline form is formed from the
  • constituent ions in the gaseous phase. However some of the ionic compounds especially alkali metal halides are formed from the
  • reaction of an alkali metal with a gaseous halogen. Therefore the lattice energy is not a quantity that can be measured direc tly. In
  • the Born–Haber cycle, the formation of an ionic solid is considered as taking place via the direct formation of the su bstance from
  • the metal and the non-metal, and the other through a series of changes from the same constituents. By Hess’s law, the energy
  • change should be the same for both processes. This means that the overall energy change in a process depends only on the
  • energy of the initial and final states, and not on the routes taken. (For correct explanation – Give 3 marks)

questions.question: A molecule of KBr has a bond length of 2.82 A˚ and an observed dipole moment of 10.41D. Calculate the percentage ionic character of the bond / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• A molecule of KBr has a bond length of 2.82 A˚ and an observed dipole moment of 10.41D. Calculate the percentage
  • ionic character of the bond
  • Bond length (r) = 2.82 Å = 2.82 × 10⁻10 m , Observed dipole moment = 10.41 D
  • Percentage ionic character = (μobs / μtheoretical) × 100
  • μtheoretical = e × r = (1.6 × 10⁻19 C) × (2.82 × 10⁻10 m) = 4.512 × 10⁻29 C·m
  • Convert to Debye: 1 D = 3.336 × 10⁻30 C·m, μtheoretical = (4.512 × 10⁻29) / (3.336 × 10⁻30) = 13.53 D
  • Percentage ionic character = (μobs / μtheoretical) × 100
  • = (10.41 / 13.53) × 100 = 76.94%
  • (Only equation – 1 mark; calculation till μtheoretical– 1.5 marks; Whole calculation till %ionic character and answer- Give 3
  • marks)

  • 2×(+0.6Δ₀) = 0.0 Δ ₀. Therefore, [Fe(CN) ₆]³⁻ gains an additional stabilization of ≈ 2.0 Δ ₀ compared to [FeF ₆]³⁻ due to ligand
